record.prompt: how does a decision tree works?

relationship.statement: A decision tree classifies data by recursively splitting samples at feature thresholds that maximize purity gain (reduction in Gini impurity), then routing new inputs down matching branches to a leaf's majority class.
assumptions: Binary classification with two equally sized classes (N = 20 samples total) along one primary feature X.
Gini impurity measures node mixedness from 0 (pure single class) to 0.5 (50/50 split).
A single decision stump splits at threshold t; deeper trees repeat this rule on each child node.

quantities.label: Split threshold t
quantities.meaning: Cutoff value on feature X sending samples left (X <= t) or right (X > t).

quantities.label: Class separation
quantities.meaning: Distance between Class A and Class B feature centers; lower values increase overlap.

quantities.label: Test sample X
quantities.meaning: Feature value of a new point routed through the decision node to a leaf prediction.

quantities.label: Total samples N
quantities.meaning: Fixed number of labeled training points split across the root node.

quantities.label: Parent Gini
quantities.meaning: Gini impurity of the unsplit root node (0 is pure, 0.5 is maximally mixed).

quantities.label: Left leaf Gini
quantities.meaning: Gini impurity of samples with X <= t routed to the left child node.

quantities.label: Right leaf Gini
quantities.meaning: Gini impurity of samples with X > t routed to the right child node.

quantities.label: Weighted child Gini
quantities.meaning: Sample-weighted average impurity of the left and right child nodes after splitting.

quantities.label: Impurity gain
quantities.meaning: Reduction in Gini impurity achieved by splitting at threshold t; higher is better.

quantities.label: Leaf confidence
quantities.meaning: Majority-class percentage in the leaf reached by the test sample X.
